name: InCharacter
ontology_notes: Personality-fidelity eval for role-playing agents, not a memory engine and not a memory bench. Wang et al. ACL 2024, arXiv 2310.17976v4. 32 characters on 14 psychological scales (BFI, 16Personalities, Dark Triad Dirty Dozen, and PsychoBench scales). Each scale item is asked as an isolated interview question so items do not contaminate each other. An LLM interviewer converts replies (option conversion) or rates like a psychiatrist (expert rating). Labels come from Personality Database plus 93 human annotations. Default RPAs are ChatHaruhi / RoleLLM with GPT-3.5. The paper also releases 18,304 interview dialogues. User modeled is a fictional character under interview. Metric scores dimensional accuracy of personality types versus human-perceived labels. Misses holes 1 as 50+ sessions (no longitudinal drift), 2 social timing, 3 joke-as-fact, 4 retcon, 5 cross-character leak, 6 lore versus lived event, 7 poisoning, 8 cost per turn, 9 forget-that, 10 three-month reunion.

supersession.evidence: Questions are posed in isolated contexts. No fact replacement over time. §3.1.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Interview items are independent. No session timestamps or reunion. §3.1.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: The RPA is a named character with descriptions and optional memory-module dialogues from ChatHaruhi or RoleLLM. That is character versus generic LLM, not user versus companion versus lore tables.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: The protocol elicits answers to every scale item. No skip or do-not-recall condition.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: No adversarial memory writes. Self-report vs interview compares method bias, not persona overwrite.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that. Character data is a static prompt plus optional dialogue snippets.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Reported number is personality alignment accuracy. No cost-per-turn meter.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: MIT LICENSE. Repo includes a pinned ChatHaruhi copy. Default path sets an OpenAI API key in config.json. personality_tests.py defaults evaluator_llm gpt-4.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Would prefer RPAs whose isolated interview answers match a character's BFI or 16P label. That is personality fidelity, not a long-term store. Not a memory bench. Would not select identity drift, silence, or poisoning of companion memory.

published_eval.name: InCharacter
published_eval.claimed_score: Abstract and Table 2. State-of-the-art RPAs reach 80.7% dimensional accuracy on 16P with expert-rating batch and GPT-4 as interviewer, against Personality Database labels. Table 7. ER_batch 80.7 Acc / 9.7 MSE on 16P PDb versus self-report 65.6 / 15.2.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether a role-playing agent's interview answers, converted to scale scores, match human-perceived personality types. Isolated psychological items. Not long-term memory, lore, or companion silence.
